name: HGS (India)
summary: HGS (India), incorporated in 1986, makes geophones, seismic cables, connectors, seismographs and other geophysical instruments at a single plant in Manesar, Haryana, mainly for oil and gas and mineral exploration, and sells to 146 clients in 21 countries. Revenue fell about 8% in FY26 to ₹45.2 cr after rising from ₹35.5 cr in FY24 to ₹49.1 cr in FY25, while profit rose 10.8% to ₹11.6 cr and the net margin widened to 25.8%. The company has no borrowings, about 69% of the ₹27.9 cr fresh issue goes to plant and machinery replacement and Manesar facility works, and the top 10 customers made up 72.6% of FY26 revenue. At the upper band the post-issue P/E is about 11.2x and price to book about 1.1x; the RHP names no listed peers.

fh1.finding: Revenue rose from ₹35.48 cr (FY24) to ₹45.16 cr (FY26), a CAGR of about 12.8%.

fh2.finding: Revenue fell in the latest year, from ₹49.08 cr in FY25 to ₹45.16 cr in FY26.

fh3.finding: Total borrowings were nil at FY26 and at April 30, 2026, so debt to equity is nil.

fh4.finding: Borrowings were nil in FY24 and FY26 (negligible in FY25), so debt did not grow while revenue rose about 27%.

fh5.finding: Net worth fell from ₹95.04 cr (FY24) to ₹85.16 cr (FY25) before rising to ₹89.27 cr (FY26).

fh6.finding: Operating cash flow was ₹6.14 cr in FY26, about 53% of the ₹11.64 cr profit.

pr1.finding: Profit after tax grew 10.8% in FY26, from ₹10.51 cr to ₹11.64 cr.

pr2.finding: PAT margin improved from 11.27% (FY24) to 21.40% (FY25) and 25.77% (FY26).

pr3.finding: Return on net worth was 13.04% in FY26.

pr4.finding: ROCE was 17.13% in FY26, up from 16.06% in FY25.

pr5.finding: The RHP says there are no listed Indian peers, so no peer margin comparison is possible.

va1.finding: Post-issue P/E is about 11.2x, but the RHP names no listed peers to compare against.

va2.finding: Post-issue price to book is about 1.1x, but there are no listed peers to compare against.

va3.finding: No listed peers, so market cap to sales cannot be compared.

va4.finding: Details of share issues or transfers in the 12 months before the IPO were not found in public sources.

pg1.finding: Promoters hold 63.50% after the issue, down from 87.30%.

pg2.finding: None of the promoter or promoter-group shares were pledged as of the RHP date.

pg3.finding: FY26 related-party payments were small (about ₹1.3 cr, mostly director pay), but the company lent ₹9.5 cr to promoter Sowar Pvt Ltd in FY24, repaid by FY25.

pg4.finding: Six direct-tax claims totalling ₹13.09 lakh are pending against promoters and directors.

is1.finding: The ₹6.65 cr offer for sale is 19.2% of the ₹34.56 cr issue.

is2.finding: The ₹34.56 cr issue is about 26.5% of the ₹130.3 cr post-issue market cap (1,08,58,713 shares at ₹120).

is3.finding: The acquisition cost of the 12 selling shareholders was not found in public sources.

up1.finding: ₹19.36 cr (69.4% of the fresh issue) goes to plant and machinery replacement, a gold-plating facility and Manesar facility works.

up2.finding: None of the fresh issue is used to repay debt.

up3.finding: ₹8.55 cr (30.6% of the fresh issue) goes to unidentified acquisitions and general corporate purposes combined; GCP alone is capped at 15%.

up4.finding: The objects include no repayment of loans to promoters or group companies.

lg1.finding: Quantified claims against the company total about ₹21 lakh (civil ₹15.28 lakh, tax ₹6.04 lakh), well under 1% of the ₹89.27 cr net worth.

lg2.finding: Case-level figures for criminal or regulatory proceedings were not found in public sources.

lg3.finding: A contingent liabilities figure was not found in public sources.

rk1.finding: The top 10 customers made up 72.58% of FY26 revenue, and the largest made up 21.79%.

rk2.finding: Imports were 73.65% of FY26 purchases, but supplier-wise shares were not found.

rk3.finding: Incorporated in 1986, so about 40 years of operating history.

rk4.finding: Auditor remarks were not found in public sources.
